big_idea: TED curator Chris Anderson argues that presentation literacy is a core skill for our era, and that any talk succeeds or fails based on whether it builds a single clear throughline of an idea worth spreading, delivered with authentic human connection.

tool.label: The throughline
tool.text: Distill the entire talk into a single connecting thread of no more than about 15 words, a rope that every story, fact, and example in the talk should visibly hang from, so the audience never loses the thread.
tool.note: Anderson's own coinage as TED's longtime curator, drawn from watching thousands of TED talks succeed or fail on structure.

ideas.title: Presentation literacy
ideas.text: Public speaking is a learnable, teachable skill with outsized career and civic impact, not a fixed talent.

ideas.title: Five tools for building a talk
ideas.text: Connection, Narration, Explanation, Persuasion, and Revelation are the core techniques for developing and delivering an idea.

ideas.title: Connect before you present
ideas.text: Open by establishing trust and common ground with the audience before diving into content.

ideas.title: Explain from the known to the unknown
ideas.text: Layer complex ideas step by step, building from what the audience already understands.

ideas.title: Persuade by demolishing objections first
ideas.text: Before presenting your case, address and dismantle the audience's likely counterarguments.

ideas.title: Visuals should support, not star
ideas.text: Use high-resolution images, minimal text, and large single typefaces so slides amplify rather than compete with the speaker.

try_it: Write your talk's throughline in 15 words or fewer before writing anything else.
Pick one of the five tools, like Narration, and rebuild your opening around it.
Cut every slide's text down to a single phrase or number, replacing paragraphs with one strong image.
Script and memorize just your first and last two sentences, even if the middle stays loose.
best_for: People preparing a specific talk or keynote
Those wanting the official TED-insider structural playbook
less_useful: Readers seeking a quick skim; some find it anecdote-heavy relative to distilled principles
Those who want techniques beyond formal stage talks, like informal pitches

related.why: A companion breakdown of what makes the most-watched TED talks land emotionally
A more compressed structure for a much shorter pitch format
